note: The G shape of CAGED: open G fretted with fingers 2, 3 and 4 (its chord box pinned, so it stays the open shape), the same shape two frets up with its arpeggio, major pentatonic and major scale, then joined to the E shape on the low E string root. The old Key selector is now moves (any key), so the text names the key only as {{=key}} and a {{?key}} line says what stays the same; each block has one feel to reach.

exercise.title: CAGED: the G shape
exercise.why: The open G chord moved up the neck fills the gap between the A shape below it and the E shape above it, and it ends on the low E string root where the E shape begins.

cells.text: Press the chord box below to hear G. Fret it as shown, but with fingers 2, 3 and 4, so finger 1 is free.

Press Play on the chord panel below to hear {{=key}} in the G shape: the open G shape moved up the neck, with finger 1 in place of the nut. The whole shape is a wide reach, so play the part of it your hand can hold.
Then press Play on the other three panels: the arpeggio, the {{=key}} major pentatonic scale and the {{=key}} major scale sit in the same frets. Play each one on your guitar, starting and ending on a root.
Practice until you can see the chord inside the scale.

Press Play on the two chord panels below to hear {{=key}} in the G shape, then in the E shape just above it. Play one, then the other, on your guitar: the root on the low E string is the same note in both, and that is where the two shapes join.
Practice until your hand finds that root from either shape.
{{?key}}In another key both shapes move along the neck and still join on the low E string.
